html:
Mikael Agricola was a Finnish clergyman who brought the Lutheran Reformation to Finland and is called the father of written Finnish.

He studied in Wittenberg under Luther and his colleague Melanchthon. Back in Turku he wrote the first book in Finnish, an ABC book, about 1543, and translated the New Testament into Finnish in 1548. To do so he had to create a way of spelling the language, based on the dialects of the southwest.

He became bishop of Turku in 1554 and died in 1557 on the way home from peace talks with Russia. His writings started Finnish literature, which grew far later into the Kalevala. 9 April, the day of his death, is the day of the Finnish language. See Finland and the Reformation.
sum: Mikael Agricola was a Finnish clergyman who brought the Lutheran Reformation to Finland and is called the father of written Finnish.
